questions.question: What is the primary purpose of general ledger (G/L) accounting?

options.A: To track the cost of overhead activities and allocate it to internal orders
options.B: To capture and record all data generated by process steps that have a financial accounting impact
options.C: To manage the purchase orders that are sent to vendors of the company
options.D: To determine how materials are produced in the work centers of a plant

questions.explanation: The G/L consists of numerous accounts that record the financial impact of business process steps.

questions.question: Into which five categories are general ledger accounts grouped?

options.A: Assets, vendors, customers, materials and expenses
options.B: Cost centers, internal orders, activity types, revenue and equity
options.C: Debits, credits, journals, ledgers and statements
options.D: Assets, liabilities, equity, revenue and expenses

questions.explanation: These five categories form the balance sheet and income statement accounts.

questions.question: Which type of account tracks obligations that will be paid off in less than one year, such as an amount owed to a tire vendor payable in 60 days?

options.A: Notes payable
options.B: Accounts payable
options.C: Retained earnings
options.D: Additional paid-in capital

questions.explanation: Notes payable tracks obligations to be paid off in more than one year (e.g., a mortgage).

questions.question: What does the retained earnings account represent?

options.A: Funds contributed by investors in addition to purchasing common stock
options.B: The amount a company owes to suppliers for materials purchased
options.C: The running total of earnings over the life of the organization
options.D: The total cost of manufacturing a product or purchasing accessories

questions.explanation: It is calculated by subtracting expenses and dividends paid to stockholders from revenue.

questions.question: How is the sales discount account classified relative to sales revenue?

options.A: As a contra account (a negative amount against sales revenue)
options.B: As an additional paid-in capital account
options.C: As a reconciliation account of the customer subledger
options.D: As an asset account that tracks inventory

questions.explanation: The original price is recorded in sales revenue and the discount amount in the sales discount account.

questions.question: Which expense account represents the total cost of manufacturing a product or purchasing accessories?

options.A: Labor expense
options.B: Supplies expense
options.C: Cost of goods sold
options.D: Advertising expense

questions.explanation: Cost of goods sold is one of the largest expenses of a company such as GBI.

questions.question: Which G/L accounts are also known as income statement accounts?

options.A: Profit and loss accounts (revenue and expense accounts)
options.B: Balance sheet accounts (assets, liabilities, equity)
options.C: Reconciliation accounts
options.D: Control accounts of the subsidiary ledger

questions.explanation: Profit and loss accounts include the revenue and expense accounts.

questions.question: Which accounts are temporary accounts that are closed at year end?

options.A: Asset, liability and equity (balance sheet) accounts
options.B: Revenue and expense (profit and loss) accounts
options.C: Reconciliation accounts only
options.D: Bank and inventory accounts only

questions.explanation: Their balances are transferred to retained earnings through the period closing technique.

questions.question: What happens to the balance sheet accounts at year end?

options.A: Their balances are transferred to the retained earnings account
options.B: Their balances are reset to zero for the next year
options.C: They are replaced by new accounts created for the following year
options.D: They are not closed; the ending balance of one year becomes the beginning balance of the next

questions.explanation: Balance sheet accounts are permanent accounts.

questions.question: If revenues exceed expenses when the profit and loss accounts are closed, the retained earnings account:

options.A: Decreases, because the company has a net loss
options.B: Stays the same, because both accounts are temporary
options.C: Becomes a liability of the company
options.D: Increases, because the company has net income

questions.explanation: If revenues are less than expenses the result is a net loss, which reduces retained earnings.

questions.question: What is period closing?

options.A: A technique to define the posting periods available in a fiscal year variant
options.B: A technique used to make adjusting entries in the general ledger to correct errors and add new entries such as depreciation
options.C: A technique that stops all users from ever posting documents again
options.D: A technique to transfer costs from cost centers to internal orders

questions.explanation: It is performed at the end of each month, quarter and year; year-end closing is the most elaborate.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the four key financial statements?

options.A: Statement of cost center variances
options.B: Statement of material movements
options.C: Statement of purchase requisitions
options.D: Statement of cash flows

questions.explanation: The four: balance sheet, income statement, statement of retained earnings, and statement of cash flows.

questions.question: Which equation guides the construction of the balance sheet?

options.A: Assets = Revenue – Expenses
options.B: Assets = Liabilities + Equity
options.C: Equity = Revenue + Liabilities
options.D: Liabilities = Assets + Equity

questions.explanation: The balance sheet is a snapshot of financial position at a point in time.

questions.question: How is net income calculated?

options.A: Assets minus liabilities
options.B: Revenue plus dividends
options.C: Revenue minus expenses
options.D: Equity minus retained earnings

questions.explanation: Net income is the difference between revenue and expenses and appears on the income statement.

questions.question: Which statement summarizes the changes in retained earnings from one year to another?

options.A: Statement of retained earnings
options.B: Balance sheet
options.C: Income statement
options.D: Statement of cash flows

questions.explanation: It starts with the beginning balance, accounts for adjustments, net income and dividends, and computes the ending balance.

questions.question: In the statement of cash flows, extending loans to customers and buying property are examples of which activities?

options.A: Operating activities
options.B: Financing activities
options.C: Investing activities
options.D: Adjusting activities

questions.explanation: Operating = A/R, A/P and daily activities; financing = cash from investors and dividends.

questions.question: Which standards does the book assume GBI uses exclusively for its financial reporting?

options.A: GAAP
options.B: IFRS
options.C: COSO
options.D: Sarbanes-Oxley

questions.explanation: The discussion is limited to GAAP, but concepts can be adapted to other standards.

questions.question: What is a subsidiary ledger (subledger)?

options.A: A part of the general ledger that contains only the profit and loss accounts
options.B: A list of accounts used to create the general ledger of a company code
options.C: A document that records the consequences of a goods receipt
options.D: A separate ledger, not part of the general ledger, used to track data for individual customers, vendors and assets

questions.explanation: Companies manage accounts payable and receivable using subledgers.

questions.question: What do control (total) accounts in the general ledger summarize?

options.A: The data of all cost centers assigned to the controlling area
options.B: The data of all the accounts in the related subledger
options.C: The postings of all company codes of the client
options.D: The master data of all materials in the plant

questions.explanation: In SAP ERP, control accounts are called reconciliation accounts.

questions.question: What are control accounts called in SAP ERP?

options.A: Clearing accounts
options.B: Contra accounts
options.C: Suspense accounts
options.D: Reconciliation accounts

questions.explanation: They include only the totals of the subledger accounts.

questions.question: A transaction with a vendor is posted. Which statement describes the postings?

options.A: The vendor account in the subledger receives a direct posting and the A/P reconciliation account receives an indirect posting
options.B: The reconciliation account receives a direct posting and the vendor account an indirect posting
options.C: Both accounts must be posted manually by the user
options.D: Only the reconciliation account is updated; the vendor account is not changed

questions.explanation: The total in the reconciliation account is updated simultaneously.

questions.question: Why are manual (direct) postings to reconciliation accounts not permitted?

options.A: Because reconciliation accounts have no company code segment in the system
options.B: Because reconciliation accounts can only be used by the controlling area
options.C: To ensure the total of the subledger accounts always equals the reconciliation account
options.D: Because they are temporary accounts closed at the end of each month

questions.explanation: The system enforces this constraint through the field "reconciliation account for account type".

questions.question: Accounts payable accounting records and manages accounting data associated with which business partners?

options.A: Vendors
options.B: Customers
options.C: Employees
options.D: Plants

questions.explanation: Accounts payable is an integral component of the procurement process (Chapter 4).

questions.question: Accounts receivable accounting is an integral component of which process?

options.A: Procurement
options.B: Production
options.C: Fulfillment
options.D: Overhead management

questions.explanation: A/R tracks customers and is discussed in the fulfillment chapter.

questions.question: How do the A/P and A/R processes compare in configuration?

options.A: A/P requires no configuration while A/R requires an extensive configuration
options.B: They share no common configuration steps at all
options.C: A/R uses a chart of accounts while A/P does not use one
options.D: They have numerous similarities and similar configuration steps

questions.explanation: The relationship of subledger and reconciliation account is identical for A/P and A/R.

questions.question: What does a company code represent?

options.A: A manufacturing or storage facility of the enterprise
options.B: The whole enterprise in the ERP system
options.C: A separate legal entity for financial accounting purposes
options.D: A group of cost centers with similar characteristics

questions.explanation: It is generally defined based on country-specific tax laws, commercial laws and other financial accounting requirements.

questions.question: How is the company code key structured?

options.A: A four-character alphanumeric key that uniquely identifies the company code
options.B: A two-digit numeric key that identifies the posting key
options.C: A ten-digit numeric key that identifies the G/L account
options.D: A six-character key that identifies the fiscal year variant

questions.explanation: It is the primary key in the tables containing company code data (e.g., US00 and DE00).

questions.question: What does the company code currency identify?

options.A: The currency used for every company code of the client
options.B: The currency used only for payments sent to vendors
options.C: The default currency used when financial data are posted to the company code
options.D: The currency of the controlling area

questions.explanation: GBI uses USD for the U.S. company code and euros for the German one.

questions.question: Which company code parameter identifies the default language for entering/displaying data and for outputs such as customer invoices?

options.A: Country key
options.B: Language
options.C: Region
options.D: Search term

questions.explanation: The system includes hundreds of standard languages.

questions.question: What does the country key of a company code define?

options.A: The currency used for all postings to the company code
options.B: The chart of accounts assigned to the company code
options.C: The number of posting periods of the fiscal year
options.D: The home country; all other countries are interpreted as abroad

questions.explanation: This lets the enterprise use different formats for transactions with other countries.

questions.question: For a company code in the United States, which additional parameter must be defined?

options.A: Transportation zone code
options.B: Tax jurisdiction code
options.C: Group chart of accounts
options.D: Posting period variant

questions.explanation: A tax jurisdiction code identifies one of many U.S. jurisdictions with their own tax regulations.

questions.question: What is the chart of accounts (CoA)?

options.A: A list of fiscal year variants available to the company codes
options.B: A list of document types generated in financial accounting
options.C: A list of cost centers used in management accounting
options.D: A list of accounts that can be used to create the general ledger

questions.explanation: The general ledger is an instance of the chart of accounts.

questions.question: Which chart of accounts is used for the day-to-day business operations?

options.A: Country-specific chart of accounts
options.B: Group chart of accounts
options.C: Operating chart of accounts
options.D: Parallel chart of accounts

questions.explanation: The operating CoA supports the company code's daily operations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a country-specific chart of accounts?

options.A: To meet legal requirements by providing the G/L accounts required for each country
options.B: To generate consolidated statements for the whole enterprise
options.C: To record the day-to-day operations of the company code
options.D: To define the fields required in G/L accounts

questions.explanation: It is chosen when a company code conducts business in countries with local legal requirements.

questions.question: Why does a company use a group chart of accounts?

options.A: To post to accounts of several countries in different currencies
options.B: To define the field status of G/L accounts for each account group
options.C: To assign document number ranges to document types
options.D: To easily generate consolidated financial statements for all company codes without manually mapping accounts

questions.explanation: It includes the G/L accounts used by all of the enterprise's company codes.

questions.question: How long can the G/L account number of a chart of accounts be?

options.A: Up to 4 digits
options.B: Up to 10 digits
options.C: Up to 6 digits only
options.D: Exactly 2 digits

questions.explanation: GBI uses six digits, which suffices for its simple ledger.

questions.question: At which level is the chart of accounts defined, and who may use it?

options.A: At the plant level; each plant needs its own chart of accounts
options.B: At the company code level; it cannot be shared between company codes
options.C: At the controlling area level; only cost accounting uses it
options.D: At the client level; one or more company codes can use it to create their general ledgers

questions.explanation: Each company code adds company code-specific data to the accounts it uses.

questions.question: Which technique allows a company to maintain multiple sets of accounting books and records?

options.A: Subledgers
options.B: Parallel ledgers
options.C: Reconciliation accounts
options.D: Posting period variants

questions.explanation: Parallel ledgers and foreign currency valuation are beyond the scope of the chapter.

questions.question: Into which smaller time intervals is a fiscal year divided?

options.A: Document types
options.B: Account groups
options.C: Number ranges
options.D: Periods (posting periods)

questions.explanation: Financial accounting postings are associated with a particular posting period.

questions.question: How many special posting periods can be defined in addition to the normal 12?

options.A: Up to 1
options.B: Up to 4
options.C: Up to 12
options.D: Up to 999

questions.explanation: Special periods record adjustments such as accruals and corrections, typically at the end of a quarter or year.

questions.question: A university fiscal year runs from August to July with four special periods. Which period number would special period 1 be?

options.A: Posting period 12
options.B: Posting period 01
options.C: Posting period 14
options.D: Posting period 13

questions.explanation: August = 01 … July = 12; special periods are 13 to 16.

questions.question: Why are postings generally allowed only in open periods?

options.A: To provide internal control by ensuring transactions are posted to the correct period
options.B: To make sure the posting period variant has exactly 12 periods
options.C: To prevent the company code from using more than one currency
options.D: To restrict the number of documents created from a number range

questions.explanation: The system permits postings in the current period and, for a few days, the previous period to correct errors.

questions.question: What does a fiscal year variant specify?

options.A: The periods that are open for postings by account type
options.B: The fields that are required for postings to G/L accounts
options.C: The start and end of the fiscal year and the number of posting periods
options.D: The range of document numbers for each document type

questions.explanation: It is a two-digit key; the number of posting periods can range from 0 to 999 and special periods from 0 to 4.

questions.question: Which fiscal year variant is described: 12 normal periods, 1 special period and a calendar year (January–December)?

options.A: K1
options.B: V9
options.D: GL00

questions.explanation: Variant 24 defines 24 half-month periods; V9 is non-year-dependent, October–September, with four special periods.

questions.question: What does a posting period variant identify?

options.A: The start and end dates of the fiscal year
options.B: The field status groups available for transactions
options.C: The periods that are available (open) for postings
options.D: The company codes assigned to a controlling area

questions.explanation: It is defined by account type, account interval and validity period.

questions.question: Which are the possible account types of a posting period variant?

options.A: Revenue, expense, asset, liability and equity
options.B: Debit, credit, special G/L, sales-related and payment
options.C: Normal, special, open, closed and reversed
options.D: Assets (A), customer (D), vendor (K), materials (M) and general ledger (S)

questions.explanation: A plus sign (+) represents all account types as a default.

questions.question: What does a plus sign (+) represent as the account type in a posting period variant?

options.A: A special period used for adjustments
options.B: A default value for all account types
options.C: A debit posting for customers
options.D: An unlimited account interval

questions.explanation: It is good practice to define one variant valid for all account types.

questions.question: Which variant must be assigned to company codes so they can use the posting periods and number of periods it defines?

options.A: Field status variant only
options.B: Account group only
options.C: Tolerance group only
options.D: Fiscal year variant and posting period variant

questions.explanation: Both variants, once created, must be assigned to one or more company codes.

topics.topicName: Field status, account groups & field groups

questions.question: What determines whether data entry is required or optional in a screen field?

options.A: The posting key only
options.B: The document number range
options.C: The field status
options.D: The fiscal year variant

questions.explanation: Field statuses are defined for G/L master data and for transactions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of account groups?

options.A: To consolidate accounts with similar characteristics so they can be managed together
options.B: To group the fields used to define the accounts
options.C: To group fields on transaction screens into field status groups
options.D: To consolidate the company codes assigned to a controlling area

questions.explanation: Account groups are created for a specific chart of accounts; a CoA can have multiple account groups.

questions.question: Which elements define an account group?

options.A: A posting key, a document type and a number range
options.B: A company code, a fiscal year variant and a currency
options.C: An account group code, a description and the range of account numbers for which it is valid
options.D: A cost element, an activity type and a settlement profile

questions.explanation: For example, balance sheet accounts range from 100000 to 399999.

questions.question: Why are subgroups of balance sheet accounts (fixed assets, liquid assets, materials, reconciliation accounts) created?

options.A: Because the chart of accounts allows only four account groups
options.B: Because they require different configuration options
options.C: Because balance sheet accounts are temporary accounts
options.D: Because they use different fiscal year variants

questions.explanation: For example, fixed assets use a subsidiary ledger and liquid assets do not.

questions.question: What are field groups in G/L account master data?

options.A: Groups of accounts with similar characteristics
options.B: Groups of field status groups assigned to a company code
options.C: Groups of posting keys defined at the client level
options.D: Groups of the fields that are used to define the accounts (e.g., account control, account management)

questions.explanation: Each field group includes individual fields whose field status must be specified.

questions.question: Which four field statuses are available for G/L account master data fields?

options.A: Required, optional and suppress only
options.B: Required, optional, display and suppress
options.C: Open, closed, blocked and released
options.D: Debit, credit, reversal and special

questions.explanation: Display fields are shown for information only and cannot be changed.

questions.question: What happens if a required field of a G/L account is left blank?

options.A: The account is created and the field is filled with a default value
options.B: The account is created but cannot be posted to
options.C: The field is suppressed automatically
options.D: The account cannot be created and the system generates an error message

questions.explanation: Optional fields can be left empty; suppressed fields are not displayed at all.

questions.question: How does a G/L account get its field statuses?

options.A: It inherits them from the posting key used in the first posting
options.B: It inherits them from the document type of the document
options.C: It inherits them from the account group it is associated with
options.D: It inherits them from the fiscal year variant of the company code

questions.explanation: The G/L account number must fall within the number range of its account group.

questions.question: How many field statuses are available for transaction fields?

options.A: Three: suppress, required and optional
options.B: Four: suppress, required, optional and display
options.C: Two: required and optional
options.D: Five: open, closed, display, required and optional

questions.explanation: The status "display" is not available for transactions.

questions.question: For transactions, fields are grouped into field groups, which are consolidated into:

options.A: Account groups, which are grouped into charts of accounts
options.B: Posting keys, which are grouped into document types
options.C: Document types, which are grouped into number ranges
options.D: Field status groups, which are grouped into field status variants

questions.explanation: The field status variant is assigned to one or more company codes.

questions.question: Which object makes the field status groups available to a company code?

options.A: The account group assigned to the G/L account
options.B: The field status variant assigned to the company code
options.C: The posting period variant of the company code
options.D: The tolerance group of the employee

questions.explanation: GBI's field status variant GL00 includes groups ZEXP, ZGBS, ZMMA, ZRAA and ZREV.

questions.question: Field status group ZEXP in the GBI example contains field groups relevant when posting to:

options.A: Revenue accounts
options.B: Bank accounts
options.C: Reconciliation accounts
options.D: Expense accounts

questions.explanation: ZREV is relevant for posting to revenue accounts.

topics.topicName: Document types, number ranges & tolerance groups

questions.question: How does the ERP system generate the unique number of each document?

options.A: From a document number range, a range of sequential numbers with a start and an end
options.B: From the posting key used in the first line item
options.C: From the fiscal year variant of the company code
options.D: From the account group of the G/L account

questions.explanation: Multiple number ranges are defined for each company code.

questions.question: A value of 9999 in the "Year" column of a document number range indicates:

options.A: The number range is valid only for the year 9999
options.B: The number range is exhausted
options.C: The document numbers are not year-specific
options.D: The number range is closed for postings

questions.explanation: If a number range is year-specific, the combination of document number and year is still unique.

questions.question: The most recent document in number range 49 (4900000000–4999999999) is 4900000122. What is the next document number?
questions.explanation: The "NR status" is the number of the last assigned document number.

questions.question: What does the document type identify?

options.A: Which fields are required in a transaction screen
options.B: Which employee posted the document
options.C: Which fiscal year the document belongs to
options.D: Which business process step generated the document

questions.explanation: Document types such as DR (customer invoice) and DZ (customer payment) are assigned number ranges.

questions.question: Which document type is generated when a customer invoice is created?

options.A: DZ
options.B: DR
options.C: KR
options.D: WE

questions.explanation: DZ is generated when a customer payment is recorded.

questions.question: The definition of a document type includes:

options.A: The posting key and the field status variant of the company code
options.B: The fiscal year variant and the posting period variant
options.C: The tolerance group of the employee and the company code currency
options.D: The account types that can be posted to and the number range for the document type

questions.explanation: For DR the permitted account types are assets, customer, material and G/L account.

questions.question: What do tolerance groups for employees specify?

options.A: The fields that are required in a posting
options.B: The upper limits on the amounts an employee can post and the payment differences permitted in postings
options.C: The periods that are open for postings
options.D: The range of G/L account numbers for an account group

questions.explanation: These limits are controls embedded in the system; if exceeded the system will not post the transaction.

questions.question: The GBI employee tolerance allows a document up to $500,000 total and $100,000 per line item. What happens if an employee tries to post a $600,000 document?

options.A: The system does not execute (post) the transaction
options.B: The system posts the document but flags it for review
options.C: The system splits the document into two documents
options.D: The system posts the document to a suspense account

questions.explanation: Exceeding a tolerance blocks the posting.

questions.question: Overpayment and underpayment tolerances in the employee tolerance group relate to which kinds of difference?

options.A: Differences between ordered and delivered quantities of materials
options.B: Differences between planned and actual production costs
options.C: Differences between the amount billed and the amount actually paid by the customer
options.D: Differences between the G/L and the subledger balances

questions.explanation: Differences are posted as a discount or to a separate gain/loss account.

questions.question: In the GBI tolerance example, how much payment difference may an employee accept?

options.A: 10% or $100, whichever is larger
options.B: 5% or $500, whichever is smaller
options.C: Any amount up to $100,000
options.D: 10% or $100, whichever is smaller

questions.explanation: Up to $10 is automatically posted as a discount if within 5% of the line item amount.

questions.question: What do the sending and paying company codes parameters for vendor payments control?

options.A: Which company code owns the chart of accounts and which owns the plants
options.B: Which company code processes vendor invoices and which one makes the payments on behalf of the enterprise
options.C: Which company code defines the posting keys and which assigns the field status
options.D: Which company code closes the periods and which prints the invoices

questions.explanation: For GBI the sending and paying company code are the same.

topics.topicName: Posting keys, automatic account determination & G/L master data

questions.question: What are posting keys?

options.A: Four-character codes that uniquely identify company codes
options.B: Two-digit numerical codes that control how line items are entered in financial accounting transactions
options.C: Ten-digit codes that identify G/L accounts
options.D: Sequential numbers that identify documents

questions.explanation: Posting keys are defined at the client level and available to all company codes.

questions.question: What does posting key 01 do?

options.A: Posts a credit entry to a vendor account when creating an invoice
options.B: Records a down payment received from a customer
options.C: Reverses a posting that was made in error
options.D: Posts a debit entry to a customer account when creating an invoice

questions.explanation: Posting key 31 posts a credit entry to a vendor account for an invoice.

questions.question: Which posting key is used to post a credit entry to a vendor account when creating an invoice?
questions.explanation: Posting key 19 is used for down payments received from customers (special G/L).

questions.question: Which two key parameters of a posting key determine how a line item is posted?

options.A: The document type and the number range
options.B: The company code and the plant
options.C: Whether it is a debit or credit posting and the account type permitted
options.D: The currency and the language

questions.explanation: Other parameters: sales-related, special G/L, reversal key and payment transaction.

questions.question: What does the special general ledger indicator of a posting key typically record?

options.A: Down payments received from a customer
options.B: Reversals of incorrect postings
options.C: Vendor invoices
options.D: Depreciation expense

questions.explanation: A down payment is a liability until the goods are delivered and invoiced.

questions.question: What does the reversal key of a posting key identify?

options.A: The document type used for reversing entries
options.B: The company code that can reverse the posting
options.C: The posting key to be used if a posting must be reversed to correct an error
options.D: The period in which reversals are allowed

questions.explanation: Reversal keys are one of the posting key parameters.

questions.question: The posting key and the document type disagree on the permitted account type. What happens?

options.A: An error results when the user attempts to post the transaction
options.B: The posting key wins and the posting is accepted
options.C: The document type wins and the posting is accepted
options.D: The system posts to a suspense account

questions.explanation: They must agree, e.g., DR and posting key 01 both permit the customer account type.

questions.question: What is the order of priority used to resolve field status conflicts between the posting key and the field status group?

options.A: Required, optional, display, suppressed
options.B: Suppressed, required, optional, display
options.C: Display, optional, required, suppressed
options.D: Optional, display, required, suppressed

questions.explanation: An error only occurs when a field is suppressed in one place and required in another.

questions.question: The posting key defines a field as optional and the field status group defines it as required. How does the system treat the field?

options.A: As an optional field
options.B: As a suppressed field
options.C: The system generates an error message
options.D: As a required field

questions.explanation: Required has priority over optional.

questions.question: What is automatic account determination (automatic account assignment)?

options.A: A technique to automatically create the chart of accounts of a company code
options.B: A technique to automatically assign employees to tolerance groups
options.C: A technique to automatically close the posting periods at year end
options.D: The mechanism that records accounting consequences behind the scenes as process steps are completed

questions.explanation: Document types, account types and posting keys are essential to it; specific rules are configured with each process.

questions.question: What is the critical master data in financial accounting?

options.A: Material master records
options.B: General ledger accounts
options.C: Cost centers
options.D: Work centers

questions.explanation: The G/L is sometimes called the heart of the ERP system.

questions.question: G/L account master data consist of which two segments?

options.A: The client segment and the plant segment
options.B: The balance sheet segment and the income statement segment
options.C: The vendor segment and the customer segment
options.D: The chart of accounts segment and the company code segment

questions.explanation: The CoA segment cannot be modified by the company code.

questions.question: Which data belong to the chart of accounts segment of a G/L account?

options.A: Currency, tax data, field status group and open item management
options.B: Account number, long and short descriptions, account group and balance sheet/income statement indicator
options.C: Line item display, post automatically only and reconciliation account type
options.D: Company code, fiscal year variant and posting period variant

questions.explanation: These are the same for all company codes using the chart of accounts.

questions.question: Which data belong to the company code segment of a G/L account?

options.A: Account number, description and account group
options.B: Document type, number range and posting key
options.C: Currency, tax-related data, field status group, open item management, line item display and reconciliation account for account type
options.D: Controlling area, cost center and activity type

questions.explanation: Each company code adds its own data (e.g., USD for GBI US, euros for GBI DE).

questions.question: For which kind of G/L account is open item management used?

options.A: Accounts such as clearing accounts where offsetting entries are matched against postings
options.B: Bank accounts, tax accounts and inventory accounts
options.C: Revenue accounts only
options.D: Reconciliation accounts only

questions.explanation: Bank, tax and inventory accounts are not managed on an open-item basis; accounts payable is.

questions.question: What does line item display allow the user to do?

options.A: Display the fields of the account in a read-only form
options.B: Create the account in more than one company code
options.C: Drill down on a G/L account to observe all of its activity
options.D: Reverse postings that were made to the account

questions.explanation: Reconciliation accounts do not use line item display; the line items are in the subledger.

questions.question: What does the "post automatically only" field prevent?

options.A: Direct (manual) postings to accounts such as inventory and material consumption accounts
options.B: Postings to periods that are closed
options.C: Postings by employees who exceed their tolerance
options.D: Postings with an invalid document type

questions.explanation: These accounts should receive postings via automatic account determination.

questions.question: How can the configuration of financial accounting be rudimentarily tested before the other processes are configured?

options.A: By creating sales orders and verifying the customer invoices
options.B: By manually posting entries to the general ledger and verifying the postings are correct
options.C: By running production orders and verifying the confirmations
options.D: By creating purchase orders and verifying the goods receipts

questions.explanation: A thorough test is not possible until the other processes (and automatic account determination) are configured.

questions.question: What are the main tasks of Financial Accounting (FI)?

options.A: Collect revenues and expenses by area of responsibility for internal management
options.B: Plan and allocate overhead costs to cost centers and internal orders
options.C: Analyze the profit of market segments using costs assigned to revenues
options.D: Post all financial transactions, keep them unchanged for reporting and produce the legal P&L statement and balance sheet

questions.explanation: FI is subject to legal requirements and reporting standards such as US GAAP, IFRS and HGB.

questions.question: Who are the stakeholders of financial accounting reports?

options.A: Internal managers who control costs and revenues
options.B: External parties such as suppliers, banks and tax authorities
options.C: Plant supervisors who coordinate production and maintenance
options.D: Project managers who budget and plan their projects

questions.explanation: Management Accounting serves internal stakeholders.

questions.question: At which level is the general ledger (G/L) managed?

options.A: The client level
options.B: The plant level
options.C: The controlling area level
options.D: The company code level

questions.explanation: Accounting-relevant transactions from Logistics or HR are posted to FI in real time through automatic account determination.

questions.question: How is every general ledger structured?

options.A: According to a chart of accounts
options.B: According to a cost center standard hierarchy
options.C: According to a profit center standard hierarchy
options.D: According to a work breakdown structure

questions.explanation: The chart of accounts contains the definitions of all G/L accounts.

questions.question: What ensures that a subledger is always reconciled with the G/L?

options.A: The subledger and the G/L are compared once at every period end
options.B: Users post the same amounts manually to both ledgers
options.C: Every subledger posting generates a corresponding posting to the assigned reconciliation G/L account
options.D: The G/L accounts of subledgers are enabled for direct posting

questions.explanation: Reconciliation accounts are not enabled for direct posting.

questions.question: Which FI component records the transactions of suppliers, and from which process does it take most of its data?

options.A: Accounts payable (AP), from the procure-to-pay process
options.B: Accounts receivable (AR), from the order-to-cash process
options.C: Asset accounting (AA), from the design-to-operate process
options.D: Bank ledger (FI-BL), from the hire-to-retire process

questions.explanation: AR takes most of its data from order-to-cash.

questions.question: What does Asset Accounting (AA) deal with?

options.A: Only fixed assets such as machines and buildings
options.B: Only the booking of cash flows of the bank accounts
options.C: Both current assets and non-current (fixed) assets
options.D: Only receivables from customers of the company

questions.explanation: The Bank Ledger (FI-BL) supports the booking of cash flows.

questions.question: Why do companies need parallel accounting (parallel valuation)?

options.A: To keep management accounting separate from legal reporting
options.B: To post every document twice in different company codes
options.C: To avoid the use of reconciliation accounts in the G/L
options.D: To compare financial statements on internationally accepted standards instead of only local principles

questions.explanation: Many companies publish statements under both local rules (US GAAP, HGB) and international standards.

questions.question: What are the two options for parallel accounting in G/L Accounting?

options.A: The leading ledger solution and the group ledger solution
options.B: The accounts solution (parallel accounts) and the ledger solution
options.C: The company code solution and the plant solution
options.D: The segment solution and the profit center solution

questions.explanation: The ledger solution is strongly recommended for new (greenfield) SAP S/4HANA systems.

questions.question: How does the accounts solution create financial statements for different accounting principles?

options.A: Several general ledgers are managed in parallel within G/L Accounting
options.B: Each principle uses its own client with a separate chart of accounts
options.C: Different valuation approaches post to different accounts, and the financial statement version evaluates the relevant accounts
options.D: Documents are split between the leading and non-leading ledgers

questions.explanation: It was formerly used often.

questions.question: What does the ledger solution in SAP S/4HANA allow?

options.A: Managing multiple general ledgers in parallel within G/L Accounting to create different financial statements
options.B: Posting different valuations to separate parallel accounts only
options.C: Assigning a different chart of accounts to every company code
options.D: Replacing the need for a leading ledger in each client

questions.explanation: G/L Accounting has one leading ledger in each client.

topics.topicName: TS410 – Organizational levels in SAP Financials

questions.question: What does a controlling area represent?

options.A: The smallest entity that supports a full legal set of books
options.B: The structure of the external market segments of the enterprise
options.C: A separate unit of cost accounting with a self-contained organizational structure for managing and allocating costs and revenues
options.D: A sub-activity of a company with its own risks and revenues

questions.explanation: Assigning more than one company code to a controlling area allows cost accounting across them.

questions.question: What must a CO area and its company codes have in common?

options.A: The same operating chart of accounts and the same fiscal year variant
options.B: The same currency and the same language
options.C: The same plant and the same cost centers
options.D: The same segment and the same profit centers

questions.explanation: Currencies can differ in cross-company-code cost accounting.

questions.question: How can accounts be linked to country-specific accounts in this setup?

options.A: By assigning a separate operating chart of accounts to each company code
options.B: By creating a new controlling area for each country
options.C: By an alternative account number (country chart of accounts) stored in the account master record
options.D: By using a different fiscal year variant for each country

questions.explanation: This preserves a common operating chart of accounts.

questions.question: What does the operating concern represent?

options.A: A separate unit of cost accounting inside one company code
options.B: The structure of the external market segments of the enterprise; several controlling areas can be assigned to it
options.C: The smallest legal unit with a full set of books
options.D: A reporting dimension for business or geographic segments

questions.explanation: Profitability Analysis (CO-PA) is used within the operating concern.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of a company code?

options.A: An organizational unit used as a reporting dimension for segment reporting
options.B: A unit of cost accounting that groups several company codes
options.C: A management-oriented unit used for internal profit control
options.D: The smallest SAP entity that supports a full legal set of books, usually within national boundaries, with a four-character key

questions.explanation: At least one company code must exist for a business to go live.

questions.question: What is a segment in General Ledger Accounting?

options.A: The smallest entity that holds a full legal set of books
options.B: An organizational unit used as a dimension for reporting, e.g., a business or geographical segment
options.C: A self-contained unit in which costs and revenues are allocated
options.D: A tool that assigns costs to the revenues of market segments

questions.explanation: Segment reporting gives insight into different business activities and improves forecasting.

questions.question: How does a business segment differ from a geographical segment?

options.A: A business segment is a country; a geographical one is a product line
options.B: A business segment is a cost center; a geographical one is a profit center
options.C: A business segment is a company code; a geographical one is a plant
options.D: A business segment is a sub-activity (product or service) with its own risks and revenues; a geographical one differs by economic or political factors

questions.explanation: International Accounting Standards (IAS) distinguish these two kinds.

topics.topicName: TS410 – G/L accounts, cost elements & account groups

questions.question: What does the chart of accounts contain for each G/L account?

options.A: The account currency and the tax code of the account
options.B: The account number, account name and type of G/L account
options.C: The cost center and the profit center of the account
options.D: The posting key and the document type of the account

questions.explanation: A chart of accounts can be used by multiple company codes so their general ledgers have an identical structure.

questions.question: What are the two segments of the G/L master record?

options.A: The balance sheet segment and the income statement segment
options.B: The controlling area segment and the cost element segment
options.C: The vendor segment and the customer segment
options.D: The chart of accounts segment and the company code segment

questions.explanation: The account definition must first be maintained at the chart of accounts level.

questions.question: What does the chart of accounts segment contain?

options.A: The account currency and tax-related settings for the company code
options.B: The account description, the account type, the account group and the consolidation account number
options.C: The posting blocks and the correspondence settings for the account
options.D: The reconciliation account and the payment terms of the account

questions.explanation: The account group controls the company code segment fields.

questions.question: Which setting is an example of a company-code-specific account setting?

options.A: The account number
options.B: The account type
options.C: The account currency
options.D: The account group

questions.explanation: E.g., company code 1010 uses EUR and company code 1710 uses USD for most accounts.

questions.question: Why is the G/L reconciliation account not enabled for direct posting?

options.A: Because reconciliation accounts only exist in the company code segment
options.B: Because they are allowed only in the leading ledger
options.C: To guarantee that the subledger and G/L are always reconciled
options.D: Because they are balance sheet accounts without a number range

questions.explanation: Postings in the G/L are limited to reconciliation account types only for subledger postings.

questions.question: How are costs defined for Management Accounting in the second (central European) approach?

options.A: Expenditures related to the business of the company, assigned to periods and valued
options.B: All expenditures in the company, regardless of their business relation
options.C: Only revenues that are related to a specific market segment
options.D: Only the expenditures that are posted to a balance sheet account

questions.explanation: A gift to a welfare organization is an expenditure but not a cost.

questions.question: What are neutral expenditures?

options.A: Costs that are posted only to statistical cost centers
options.B: Expenditures that do not meet the definition of costs and are only reflected in Financials
options.C: Costs that are allocated to several controlling areas
options.D: Revenues that are posted to non-operating income accounts

questions.explanation: They do not appear in Management Accounting.

questions.question: Which G/L account type is carried forward at the fiscal year end?

options.A: Primary costs or revenue
options.B: Secondary costs
options.C: Non-operating expense or income
options.D: Balance sheet

questions.explanation: Income statement accounts are closed.

questions.question: Which G/L account type functions as a cost element for operating expenses such as payroll and selling expenses?

options.A: Secondary costs
options.B: Cash account
options.C: Non-operating expense or income
options.D: Primary costs or revenue

questions.explanation: Secondary costs arise from internal value flows.

questions.question: Which G/L account type functions as a cost element for internal activity allocations, overhead allocations and settlements?

options.A: Primary costs or revenue
options.B: Secondary costs
options.C: Cash account
options.D: Balance sheet

questions.explanation: Secondary costs result from value flows within the organization.

questions.question: What is the benefit of a cash account type?

options.A: It carries the balance forward to the next fiscal year automatically
options.B: It functions as a cost element for secondary costs
options.C: It allows direct posting to reconciliation accounts
options.D: One G/L account can be assigned to more than one house bank account, reducing the number of G/L accounts

questions.explanation: A G/L account is otherwise required for each house bank account.

questions.question: For which G/L accounts is controlling-area-specific data needed?

options.A: Balance sheet accounts and cash accounts
options.B: Secondary costs and primary costs or revenue accounts, where a cost element category is assigned
options.C: Reconciliation accounts only
options.D: Every G/L account of the chart of accounts

questions.explanation: The cost element category determines which account can be used for which business transaction in CO.

topics.topicName: TS410 – G/L document posting & business partners

questions.question: What are the main parts of an accounting document?

options.A: A document header and line items
options.B: A vendor line and a customer line
options.C: A debit part and a credit part posted separately
options.D: A budget part and an actual part

questions.explanation: The entry view allows a maximum of 999 line items.

questions.question: Which fields uniquely identify an accounting document?

options.A: Document number, posting key and document type
options.B: Posting date, plant and cost center
options.C: Document number, company code and fiscal year
options.D: Company code, controlling area and profit center

questions.explanation: Document numbers come from number ranges assigned to document types.

questions.question: Which two control keys are important in an accounting document?

options.A: The document type (header) and the posting key (line items)
options.B: The company code (header) and the fiscal year (line items)
options.C: The posting date (header) and the account type (line items)
options.D: The reference number (header) and the profit center (line items)

questions.explanation: Document types distinguish and order the various accounting documents.

questions.question: What does a posting key control for a line item?

options.A: The company code and the fiscal year of the document
options.B: The document number range and the document type
options.C: The profit center and the segment of the line item
options.D: The account type to be posted, the type of posting (debit or credit) and the field statuses

questions.explanation: Each line item contains one posting key.

questions.question: In the Fiori app Post General Journal Entries, which posting keys do debit and credit correspond to?

options.A: Debit = 50, credit = 40
options.B: Debit = 40, credit = 50
options.C: Debit = 01, credit = 31
options.D: Debit = 89, credit = 99

questions.explanation: In selected transactions (e.g., FB50) the posting key no longer has to be entered.

questions.question: What do journal entry templates allow?

options.A: Posting entries automatically at each period end
options.B: Reversing an entry that was posted in error
options.C: Splitting an entry across several company codes
options.D: Saving time by pre-selecting fields and values for numerous similar journal entries; templates can be shared publicly

questions.explanation: They are created with the Manage Journal Entry Templates app.

questions.question: In SAP S/4HANA, which master record is used to manage vendors?

options.A: The vendor master record in the MM component only
options.B: The business partner, which is the single point of entry for business partners, customers and vendors
options.C: The customer master record with a vendor indicator
options.D: The cost center master with a vendor assignment

questions.explanation: Application-neutral data such as name, address and bank details is stored in the general data.

questions.question: What does a business partner role represent?

options.A: A business context in which the partner appears and which provides the application-specific data, e.g., FI Vendor, FI Customer, Supplier
options.B: A natural person, group or organization classification
options.C: The grouping that determines the number range
options.D: The company code in which the partner is used

questions.explanation: The role FI Vendor allows company-code-specific data for Accounts Payable.

questions.question: What does the business partner category classify?

options.A: The partner as a vendor, customer or prospect
options.B: The partner as external or internal
options.C: The partner as a natural person, a group or an organization, which determines the available fields
options.D: The partner as a domestic or foreign company

questions.explanation: For an organization, the legal form can be entered.

questions.question: What does the business partner grouping determine, and can it be changed?

options.A: The business partner role; it can be changed at any time
options.B: The company code; it can be changed at any time
options.C: The account group; it cannot be changed
options.D: The number range (internal/external); it cannot be changed afterwards

questions.explanation: Groupings are defined in Customizing together with their number ranges.

questions.question: Which data does the company code segment of a vendor contain?

options.A: Name, address and bank details of the vendor
options.B: Reconciliation account, terms of payment, payment methods, dunning data, correspondence settings and posting blocks
options.C: Purchasing organization and incoterms of the vendor
options.D: Tax jurisdiction and general data of the vendor

questions.explanation: A company must create a company code segment to do business with a vendor.

questions.question: Why is document splitting used?

options.A: To post one document to several company codes in different currencies
options.B: To separate FI documents from CO documents in the Universal Journal
options.C: To limit each document to a maximum of 999 line items
options.D: To get an accurate balance sheet per segment, because otherwise the vendor line has no segment and segments only receive the expense posting

questions.explanation: Customizing can specify that the system completes the missing entries automatically.
